original_text: - **UNB-SUCC-008:** Succession activation SHALL atomically or recoverably suspend/revoke former advisory authority, establish successor permissions, enforce open-grant and standing-instruction policies, and preserve pending commitments and restrictions.
statement: The system MUST split authority transition on a death or incapacity notice into three independently recorded steps. (1) ProtectiveHold, on any notice: blocks new recommendations, recurring-instance releases and contact or payee changes for rights derived from the subject party. (2) DerivedRightsSuspended, on verified evidence: suspends every session, credential binding, delegated agent principal and privilege derived from the subject party. (3) SuccessionActivated, on sponsor approval: grants successor rights. Steps 2 and 3 MUST each be atomic within the authoritative store. Rights of other participants that do not derive from the subject MUST remain in force.
business_objective: Close the window in which a deceased or incapacitated party's authority can be exercised, without disrupting independent co-advisors or pre-empting the sponsor's decision.
preconditions: fund exists with versioned participant relationships (UNB-PART-004)
inputs: SuccessionTriggerReported(evidence refs, notifier identity, assurance level)
processing_rules: On SuccessionTriggerReported at any assurance level, append ProtectiveHoldPlaced scoped to rights whose authority chain includes the subject party.
ProtectiveHold blocks new recommendation submission, release of recurring instances and sensitive profile changes. It does not cancel anything.

On SuccessionTriggerVerified, in one transaction: append DerivedRightsSuspended; revoke sessions and credential bindings for the subject and for agent principals delegated by the subject; and mark pending unapproved recommendations from the subject as Held.
Pending sponsor-approved grants follow death_pending_grant_policy (RR-REQ-X-008-r1). They are not altered by this step.
SuccessionActivated requires sponsor approval, references the SuccessionPlan version and evidence snapshot, and grants successor rights from the approved effective time.
If the trigger is later corrected as false, append ProtectiveHoldReleased or RightsReinstated. Never delete the suspension history.
postconditions: No command authorized solely through the subject party's authority chain succeeds after DerivedRightsSuspended.
Rights of non-derived co-advisors are unchanged.
Every suspended item stays reconstructible as-of any time.
failure_behavior: If session revocation fails at the identity provider, the domain-level authorization check still denies, and an incident is raised.
If evidence conflicts, the case moves to Disputed and the hold persists.
security: Notice submission is rate-limited and authenticated where possible.
Step-up verification is required for anyone lifting a hold.
No self-approval: a notifier who is also a successor-designate cannot verify the notice.
auditability: Immutable events with actor, evidence hash, policy version and effective/recorded times.
Affected-actions report retained with the case.
configuration: Sponsor MAY configure evidence types accepted for verification (owner: GC).
Sponsor MAY configure which actions ProtectiveHold blocks, provided recommendation submission and payee/contact changes are always included. Not configurable: suspension on verified evidence.

advisory: extract fields from death certificates and court letters for human comparison
autonomous: place ProtectiveHold (deterministic rule on notice receipt)
ai_assistance.human_approval_boundary: Verification and activation are human or sponsor-authorized. AI output is evidence only.

ui_implications: Co-advisor view shows a neutral 'fund under review' banner without disclosing the reason unless policy permits.
Notifier receives a receipt and the next steps.
api_implications: Command ReportSuccessionTrigger (idempotency key = notifier + subject + evidence hash).
reporting_implications: Open succession cases with age.
Count of blocked actions.

original_text: **Normative proposed requirement:** Donor death does not automatically cancel valid sponsor-approved unpaid grants; future instructions suspend until successor authority verified; each recurring instance rechecks authority and eligibility.
statement: On verified death of a party, the disposition of that party's pending items MUST follow the sponsor's versioned death_pending_grant_policy. The policy sets one value for sponsor-approved unpaid grants (complete | hold_for_review | cancel_by_sponsor_decision), one for unapproved recommendations (lapse | hold), and one for recurring templates (suspend). Each recurring instance MUST re-check current authority and eligibility at release. Rights of other participants that do not derive from the deceased MUST NOT be suspended. Default (RCD-022, RCD-039): sponsor-approved unpaid grants complete unless the sponsor policy value is hold_for_review or cancel_by_sponsor_decision. (Integration amendment 2026-11-23; replaces the interim hold_for_review default.)
business_objective: Apply the sponsor's own governing decision to pending grants after a death, consistently and auditably.
preconditions: policy version effective at verification time
inputs: pending grant set with approval state
processing_rules: Classify each pending item by state: Approved-unpaid, Submitted-unapproved, RecurringTemplate, InstanceScheduled.
Apply the policy value per class. If the policy is unset, default to hold_for_review for every class.
Completing an approved grant requires no new donor action but MUST re-run eligibility, sanctions and capacity checks at release.
Cancelling an approved grant requires a recorded sponsor decision. It is never automatic.
Recurring instances after verification are not released. Templates are suspended pending successor authority.
postconditions: Every pending item has exactly one disposition that references the policy version.
failure_behavior: Policy lookup failure leads to hold_for_review.
security: Only sponsor-authorized roles may change the policy (A4).
auditability: Disposition events are linked to the case and the policy version.
configuration: Sponsor MUST choose a value per class (owner: sponsor board + GC). The hold_for_review default is not configurable until OD-03 is decided.

advisory: list affected items and draft charity notifications
autonomous: deterministic classification and application of the chosen policy
ai_assistance.human_approval_boundary: Policy selection and any cancellation are A4 sponsor decisions.

ui_implications: Successor and estate see the disposition of each pending item with its reason.
reporting_implications: Grants completed after death are reported normally. The death flag is used only for internal analytics.

acceptance_criteria.then: the grant is held by the eligibility check, not paid

reason_for_change: The original encodes an unanswered owner decision and is ambiguous for multi-participant funds.

tradeoffs: Hold-by-default delays charities until the sponsor decides.
regulatory_implications: Needs counsel and board: OD-03.

original_text: - **UNB-SUCC-004:** A succession plan MAY specify fractional or amount-based allocations to multiple successor accounts, subject to approved minimums, restrictions, liquidity and valuation rules. Allocations must be deterministic, auditable and reconcile exactly; no assumed automatic division.
statement: A successor allocation MUST be computed by a deterministic, versioned algorithm. Inputs: the approved plan; one sponsor-designated valuation point; the fund's available capacity net of reservations, accrued fees and approved-unpaid grants; and per-position divisibility. The algorithm MUST express shares in the fund's unit of account. It MUST assign any rounding residual by a declared rule. It MUST post one balanced allocation journal whose successor credits sum exactly to the origin debit, and MUST hold the split for sponsor decision when any constraint (minimum, restriction, illiquidity, open commitment) cannot be met.
business_objective: Make multi-successor splits reproducible and exactly reconciled.
preconditions: no open Unknown payment attempts on the origin fund
close of period not locked for the posting date
inputs: plan allocation (percent or amount per successor)
processing_rules: Compute distributable capacity C as the value at the valuation point, minus reservations, minus accrued fees, minus approved-unpaid grants that the policy says to complete.
Amount-based allocations are satisfied first in plan priority order. Percentages then apply to the remainder.
Round each share down to the smallest currency or unit increment. Assign the residual to the successor ranked first in plan priority (configurable rule).
Divisible positions are allocated pro rata in kind if policy allows; otherwise they are liquidated under sponsor approval before allocation.
If any successor share is below the account minimum, or a restriction cannot follow, place the split on SplitHeld for sponsor decision.
Trailing receipts and returns after the split are routed by the sponsor parameter trailing_receipt_destination (OD-11).
postconditions: Sum of successor credits equals origin debit exactly.
Origin fund is closed or retains only the declared residual.
failure_behavior: Valuation is unavailable or stale: hold.
Replay: the idempotency key (case id + plan version) prevents a duplicate posting.
security: Allocation and approval by different actors (SoD).
auditability: Preview, inputs, algorithm version and journal are linked.
configuration: Sponsor MAY configure valuation point (decision date | posting date | specific close), residual rule, in-kind permission and trailing-receipt destination (owner: CFO). Not configurable: exact balancing.

ai_assistance.human_approval_boundary: Sponsor approves posting.

ui_implications: Preview table showing each successor's share, residual line and held reasons; accessible tabular alternative to graph (UNB-SUCC-013).
reporting_implications: Internal allocation is not a grant and not a contribution for Schedule D purposes, pending CPA confirmation.

tradeoffs: The residual rule favors one successor by at most one minor unit.
regulatory_implications: Needs CPA: classification of internal allocations versus grants.

original_text: - **UNB-PART-007:** Onboarding SHALL support invitation, acceptance, identity verification, declined invitation, inactive status and removal without deleting history.
statement: Participant onboarding MUST record identity-related checks as four separately classified obligations, each with an authority type and owner: (a) sanctions screening; (b) identity proofing at a sponsor-configured assurance level for authentication and fraud control; (c) any customer-identification or AML program, enabled only when counsel records that it applies, by law or by contract with a custodian or payment provider; (d) source-of-funds or gift-acceptance diligence under sponsor policy. The system MUST NOT label any check 'KYC' or 'legally required' without a linked applicability record.
business_objective: Collect only the identity data that the applicable authority justifies, and make failure outcomes deterministic.
preconditions: invitation issued by an authorized participant or sponsor
processing_rules: Resolve the applicable regimes from the applicability register for (sponsor, role, channel).
Run only the enabled regimes. Store raw identity evidence in the segregated identity vault, and keep only references and outcomes in authoritative events (UNB-DATA-007).
Outcome per regime is Pass, Fail, Refer or Unavailable. Unavailable never equals Pass.
Role activation requires every enabled regime to be Pass, or Refer resolved by an authorized human.
If a contribution arrived before a Fail, apply the sponsor's failed_identity_contribution_policy. The fund never becomes grantable until resolved (TVF-113).
postconditions: No role activates with a Fail or unresolved Refer.
Declined or removed invitations retain history.
failure_behavior: Provider outage: role remains pending; the invitee is told which step is pending, without exposing screening details.
security: Sanctions match details are visible only to compliance roles.
Vault access is logged.
auditability: Every check records the regime, authority type, provider, version and reviewer.
configuration: Sponsor MAY configure the assurance level for (b) and the scope of (d) (owner: CRCO). Regime (c) can be enabled only through a counsel applicability record (owner: GC). Not configurable: (a) where counsel records it as applicable.

ai_assistance.human_approval_boundary: Refer resolution by compliance roles (A4 for sanctions).

ui_implications: Plain-language reason for each requested document.
Accessible alternative proofing channel.
reporting_implications: Onboarding funnel by regime and outcome, without personal data.

statement: The relationship model MUST provide distinct role types, each independently assignable, overlapping only by explicit grant: contributor; advisory-privilege holder (original or additional); authorized viewer; administrative contact; professional advisor; successor advisor; successor-designate; legal representative (subtypes: agent under power of attorney, guardian/conservator, personal representative/executor, trustee, entity authorized signatory); and sponsor staff. original_text: UNB-WF-015: Dormant accounts (WF-15) SHALL follow approved notice, successor and charitable-default policies.
statement: Fund inactivity MUST be governed by a sponsor-approved, versioned dormancy policy. Parameters: the activity events that reset the clock; Quiet, Inactive and Unresponsive thresholds; required outreach channels and attempts; and the default disposition (charitable default to sponsor-designated purposes or charities, transfer to a donor-named charitable beneficiary under UNB-SUCC-011, or continued holding). The lifecycle is Active > Quiet > Inactive > Unresponsive > DispositionPending > Disposed or Reactivated. Any disposition distributing assets MUST be an A4 sponsor decision run through the normal grant lifecycle. Escheat handling MUST NOT apply to fund balances unless counsel records it as applicable.
business_objective: Resolve dormant funds lawfully and consistently, without coercive or conflicted nudging.
processing_rules: The clock resets on any event in the policy's activity set (grant recommendation, login with authenticated action, contribution, explicit 'keep active' affirmation).
Each threshold transition is deterministic and appends an event.
Outreach goes to every verified channel of every advisory-privilege holder and successor-designate. Each attempt and its delivery evidence are recorded.
Any authorized activity before Disposed returns the fund to Active.
Disposition creates grant recommendations attributed to the sponsor-policy actor. These grants follow the normal eligibility and approval lifecycle.
postconditions: No disposition without documented outreach meeting policy minimums.
failure_behavior: Undeliverable channels are recorded. Disposition still requires the minimum number of documented attempts.
security: Dormancy reminders must not recommend recipients in which the sponsor or platform has a financial interest.
auditability: Full outreach history retained.
configuration: Sponsor MUST set thresholds and disposition (owner: sponsor board). Not configurable: an A4 decision before any distribution.

advisory: suggest charities from the donor's own history only

statement: A donor-recommended transfer of all or part of a fund to another sponsoring organization MUST be processed as a sponsor distribution through the standard grant lifecycle, with purpose code DAF_TRANSFER_OUT, unless counsel records a different classification. statement: Institutional migration MUST run as a MigrationRun through Contracted > Inventoried > Mapped > ImportedToStaging > Reconciled > ParallelValidated > CutoverAuthorized > SingleWriterActive > PostCutoverVerified > Archived. security: Import files are integrity-checked and signed.

original_text: - **UNB-ACC-006:** Record contribution lifecycle from intent through receipt, valuation, restrictions, acceptance, acknowledgment, settlement and disposition, with distinct cash, securities and complex noncash treatments.
statement: Unbound MUST record each contribution as distinct, timestamped facts: Intent, Received (by rail), CompletedGiftDetermined, SponsorAccepted, Valued (separate typed values: sponsor book value, custody receipt value, optional informational acknowledgment value, sale proceeds), Acknowledged, Settled/Final, and Disposed. Acknowledged MUST NOT occur before CompletedGiftDetermined and SponsorAccepted. Grantable capacity MUST NOT increase before Final (RCD-019, RCD-033; provisional credit is not offered in release 1).
business_objective: Produce lawful, correct donor substantiation and correct fund value without acknowledging or spending gifts that do not complete.
actors: Sponsor gift acceptance officer (or delegated policy)
preconditions: Counsel-approved acknowledgment template version exists for the sponsor
processing_rules: Completed-gift date = rule(assetType, rail, evidence) from a versioned table (UNB-RCN-FIN-012); missing evidence => state stays Received
Acceptance uses sponsor gift-acceptance policy by asset class; complex assets require specialist decision (CTL-021)
Acknowledgment issuance is a separate command gated on CompletedGiftDetermined AND SponsorAccepted AND template validation (UNB-RCN-FIN-001)
Capacity contribution = settled value for final rails; provisional value only within the OD-04 limit
Every fact is append-only with effective and recorded times

(merged from REG draft) Acknowledgment content:  a written acknowledgment for every contribution that (a) states the amount of cash or a description (not a value) of noncash property, (b) states whether any goods or services were provided and, if so, a good-faith estimate of their value, and (c) states that the sponsoring organization has exclusive legal control over the contributed assets (IRC 170(f)(18)(B)). For noncash property it MUST track Form 8283 Section B donee signature requests and every disposition within 3 years of receipt that requires a Form 8282 (filed within 125 days, copy to donor).
postconditions: No acknowledgment exists for a contribution lacking CompletedGiftDetermined and SponsorAccepted
Sum of fund contribution facts reconciles to GL contribution accounts per fund
The four noncash values are never overwritten by each other
failure_behavior: Missing evidence => Received, with an exception case
Template validation fails => issuance blocked, case to Controller
Rail return after acknowledgment => ReturnedContributionExposure fact plus acknowledgment void/correction workflow; original preserved
security: Tenant, sponsor and fund scoping on every command
Donor cannot self-accept
Acknowledgment content changes require counsel-approved template version
auditability: Each fact stores actor, policy version, evidence hash, effective and recorded times
Acknowledgment links to the exact contribution facts and template version
configuration: Sponsor: accepted asset classes and rails
Sponsor: provisional-credit limit (OD-04, owner sponsor CFO)

original_text: **Ordering:** Global charity/hold publication and payment release must have a provable serialization point. Holds are binding on releases ordered after their durable commit. A preexisting release intent is not the same as irreversible external submission; dispatch rechecks holds where possible. Post-submission holds cannot guarantee reversal. statement: Each global hold (charity, sanctions, recipient) MUST be committed in the hold registry with a strictly increasing HoldPublicationVersion. A payment release in any cell MUST, inside the release transaction, obtain the registry's current HoldPublicationVersion and verify that the recipient has no active hold at that version; it MUST record that version on the release. If the registry is unreachable or the cell's replicated watermark is behind the registry version, the release MUST remain in ReleaseBlocked and MUST NOT be dispatched. Dispatch MUST re-check holds immediately before irreversible external submission.
business_objective: Guarantee that no payment is released to a recipient held before the release committed, across separated tenant stores.

processing_rules: Read registry version V and recipient hold status at V within the release gate.
If any active hold applies at V: transition grant payment to Held(reason=hold ID).
If registry unavailable: ReleaseBlocked(reason=HOLD_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE); retry with bounded backoff.
Record V on ReleaseAuthorized.
At dispatch: re-read registry; if a hold with version > V applies, do not submit; transition to Held.
postconditions: For every dispatched payment, no hold active at dispatch time for that recipient
Each release records the hold version it observed

original_text: **Proposed:** Every public API operation, input field, configuration property, workflow action, dashboard widget and email block/token MUST expose authoritative, versioned, machine-readable AI assistance metadata covering purpose, types, dependencies, valid values, policy, permissions, side effects, errors, Unknown states, examples, source provenance and safe guidance. Required core fields: contractId (stable URN), version (semver), ownerComponent, kind (enum: apiOperation|configProperty|workflowAction|uiField|templateToken), purpose (text, max 280 chars), inputSchemaRef, outputSchemaRef, sideEffects (enum list: none|createsDraft|changesConfig|changesAuthoritativeState|externalEffect), authorityClass (A0..A5 per GOV authority tiers), confirmationRequired (bool), reversibility (enum: reversible|compensatable|irreversible), unknownStates (list), errors (list of error codes), visibility (enum: public|tenantScoped|roleScoped|restricted). original_text: Unbound maintains one authoritative, standardized charity-vetting framework and reusable evidence/status across sponsors. A vetted charity does not undergo duplicate routine vetting solely because another sponsor uses it. Record scope, evidence provenance, effective date and expiry; reverify at least every 180 days, on material changes, and check current sanctions/eligibility at execution. Adverse findings propagate to all affected sponsors. Sponsor-specific grant restrictions and approvals remain distinct from common charity vetting; no self-approved vetting exceptions. Cross-sponsor legal reliance, liability, jurisdictions and recipient classes require counsel validation; model never clears holds.
statement: For every grant, the system MUST evaluate recipient eligibility at two points, approval and payment release, against (a) a current IRS-status observation (TEOS/Pub 78 or EO BMF, plus the Auto-Revocation List) whose retrieval timestamp is no older than the sponsor-configured status-freshness window, and (b) current sanctions screening. It MUST store a per-sponsor, per-grant immutable snapshot of that observation containing the fields required by Rev. Proc. 2018-32 §8.01. A shared cross-sponsor charity evidence record MAY be reused as an input, but each sponsor's reliance snapshot MUST be written to that sponsor's partition. A comprehensive charity review (deep vetting) MUST occur at the sponsor-configured deep-review interval (default 180 days, a sponsor policy and not a legal safe harbor) and on any material-change signal. An expired deep review MUST hold new approvals but MUST NOT be the sole basis for payment-time eligibility.
business_objective: Avoid taxable distributions under IRC 4966 by preserving the sponsor's grant-date reliance under Rev. Proc. 2018-32, while not repeating costly deep vetting for every sponsor.

Sponsor policy version active, defining status_freshness_window and deep_review_interval

Eligible only if the observation shows 509(a)(1)/(2)/(3) public charity status AND not on the Auto-Revocation List AND (if 509(a)(3)) a type that is not non-functionally-integrated Type III AND a current donor-control certification exists for Type I/II/FI-III.
Any recipient outside the excepted classes is routed to expenditure-responsibility or rejection; never auto-approved.
Sanctions: a potential match produces Hold; only an authorized human may disposition a potential match; AI may summarize evidence only.

original_text: Retain all financial documents and substantiating financial evidence for **at least seven years**, with longer applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, sponsor or litigation-hold requirements taking precedence. This is a nonwaivable platform floor, not a legal conclusion that all records can be deleted after seven years. Retention clocks must be approved per record class; fund closure, donor death, advisor change and sponsor offboarding do not shorten retention. Originals and corrections remain immutable and linked; legal holds apply to existing and future matching evidence. Expiry triggers governed disposition review, never automatic deletion.
statement: Every stored record MUST be assigned exactly one retention class at creation. Each class MUST declare its authority (statute, regulation, contract, sponsor policy), trigger event, and minimum period. The effective retention of a record MUST be the maximum over all applicable classes, the platform floor (7 years from trigger, sponsor policy) and any legal hold. At minimum the catalog MUST include: OFAC/sanctions records (10 years from the transaction or screening decision, 31 CFR 501.601); tax-reliance snapshots (≥ the platform floor and until the related return period is closed, per counsel Q5); cost-basis and carryover records (until 7 years after the final disposition the record substantiates); and personal data not required as a financial record (deletable on request after its financial-record role ends). Expiry MUST create a disposition review task; deletion MUST NOT occur automatically.

original_text: - **UNB-PLAT-007:** **Strata** SHALL be used in the persistence architecture. All authoritative business history is append-only; corrections and reversals append new records. Physical storage guarantees and Strata integration must be verified.
statement: Authoritative business history MUST be stored by an Unbound-owned Ledger/Event Store component on managed PostgreSQL, in which authoritative tables are insert-only for the application role (no UPDATE/DELETE grants), corrections and reversals are new linked records, and each append is assigned a per-stream sequence number checked under optimistic concurrency. Strata MUST be used as the schema governance layer: every schema object for the authoritative store, including grants, triggers and row-level-security policies that enforce append-only and tenant isolation, MUST be declared in Strata source, deployed only through Strata plans, and checked for drift before each release; a 'not-compared' or 'unverifiable' Strata state for any such object MUST block release.
business_objective: Keep tamper-resistant, reconstructable financial and authority history without assuming capabilities Strata does not have.
processing_rules: Application role holds INSERT and SELECT only on authoritative tables
Append = (streamId, expectedVersion, events); mismatch → ConcurrencyConflict
Break-glass role use raises an incident and is logged outside the database
postconditions: No UPDATE or DELETE on authoritative tables by the application role
Drift report shows 'matches' for every governed object before release
failure_behavior: Drift detected in production: release blocked; incident opened
Strata reports not-compared for a policy: treated as failure, not pass
security: RLS policies by tenant on every authoritative table (see tenancy decision RCD-004)
auditability: Strata signed artifacts retained per release
Hash chain over each stream (Unbound-owned) for tamper evidence
configuration: not configurable: integrity property

advisory: Explain a Strata plan or drift report
